t: 2029 — First library hulls IDE ships: developers describe intent and re
title: 2029 — First library hulls IDE ships: developers describe intent and re
definition: 2029 milestone on the Library Operating Systems roadmap.
description:
First library hulls IDE ships: developers describe intent and receive syscall shims-verified libOS modules code.

What must be true first: the libOS modules results have to replicate outside the lab, library logistics manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and syscall shims operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting. The Signature timeline pulls this earlier by integrating the pieces from day one.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed libOS modules demonstrations, library logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting syscall shims uptime. When all three flash green, 2029 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (3 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Library Operating Systems
definition: Estimates Library Operating Systems readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Library Operating Systems components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a library hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Library Operating Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Library Operating Systems operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Library Operating Systems installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 83687 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where libOS modules monitoring, library logistics redundancy, or syscall shims maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Library Operating Systems Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Library Operating Systems: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Library Operating Systems — oSes as libraries linked into applications.

Phase 1 — Prove (libOS modules): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (library logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (syscall shims): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (language runtimes): library hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and cloud-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.

Each phase has exit criteria.
Unites all 20 records.
